title: What أَنْ Does to Every Verb Form — a fatḥa, a Dropped نُون, or Nothing at All
summary: An entire session on one rule, worked across the whole paradigm. After أَنْ a singular verb simply takes a fatḥa; any form ending in a نُون — the masculine plural, the feminine singular you, and the dual — loses that نُون instead; and the feminine plural, carrying نُون النِّسْوَة, refuses to change at all. The teacher's Qur'ānic anchor is Pharaoh's chiefs saying يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ, where the dual نُون has fallen away, and he notes that لَام التَّعْلِيل behaves in exactly the same way.
key_points: After أَنْ a singular verb takes a fatḥa: يَذْهَبُ becomes أَنْ يَذْهَبَ.

Where the verb ends in a نُون there is no room for a fatḥa, so the نُون is dropped: يَذْهَبُونَ becomes أَنْ يَذْهَبُوا, تَذْهَبِينَ becomes أَنْ تَذْهَبِي, and the dual يَذْهَبَانِ becomes أَنْ يَذْهَبَا.
So in practice أَنْ has only two possible effects — add a fatḥa, or remove the نُون.

The one exception is نُون النِّسْوَة. يَذْهَبْنَ and تَذْهَبْنَ do not change for أَنْ or for anything else. A single female is still open to change (تَذْهَبِي), but once the subject is a group of women the form is fixed.
When the نُون is dropped from a masculine plural, a small alif is written at the end — يَذْهَبُوا — purely as a spelling convention.
لَام التَّعْلِيل follows the identical rule, since it too puts the verb into the accusative: لِيَعْلَمُوا rather than لِيَعْلَمُونَ, while لِيَذْهَبْنَ keeps its نُون.
The earlier rule still holds alongside this: a verb placed before a plural doer stays singular — تُرِيدُ الْبَنَاتُ — but reversed, الْبَنَاتُ يُرِدْنَ takes the plural.
When speaking about someone rather than as them, every pronoun must shift: مَعِي becomes مَعَ بَنَاتِهِ.
أَنَا اسْمِي is incorrect — it says I, my name is. اسْمِي alone already means my name is, because the subject is the name, not the speaker.
هَؤُلَاءِ can be redundant where the subject is already clear from context, but it is needed when it would otherwise be unclear who they refers to.

بُكْرَة literally means the early part of the morning, and because morning begins the day it comes to mean tomorrow. مُبَكِّر means early, and the Prophet ﷺ supplicated اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لِأُمَّتِي فِي بُكُورِهَا — so there is barakah in what is done early.
مَكْتَب is an office while مَكْتَبَة is a library or bookshop.

Vocabulary: حَدِيقَة الْحَيَوَانَات (zoo), مَتْحَف (museum), حِصَّة (a class period), مَهَاجِع (dormitories), ضَوْضَاء (noise), صَيْدَلِيَّة (pharmacy), الْغَدَاء (lunch) against غَدًا (tomorrow), and عِيَادَة for visiting the sick.
questions: [00:02:00] Q: Why is it تُرِيدُ rather than the plural, when the subject is plural? — A: Because the verb comes before its doer, and in that order it stays singular. Reversed — الْبَنَاتُ يُرِدْنَ — it would be plural.
[00:10:00] Q: Shouldn't it be مَعِي? — A: Only if you were Ḥāmid. Since we are speaking about him, it becomes مَعَ بَنَاتِهِ.
[00:12:00] Q: What exactly does أَنْ do to a plural verb? — A: It cannot add a fatḥa to an ending already fixed, so it drops the نُون — يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَسْكُنُوا, not يَسْكُنُونَ.
[00:16:01] Q: Is هَؤُلَاءِ redundant in that sentence? — A: It can be, if the subject is already clear; but if it is not obvious who is meant, it belongs there.
[00:17:00] Q: Is أَنَا اسْمِي acceptable, as people say? — A: No, it is plainly wrong. اسْمِي already means my name is; adding أَنَا makes it I, my name is.
[00:22:00] Q: Does the dual also drop its نُون? — A: Yes. يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَا in Sūrat Ṭāhā shows it: the original would be يُخْرِجَانِ.
[00:26:00] Q: Does a single female change after أَنْ? — A: Yes, she does — تَذْهَبِي. It is only the feminine plural that is immune.
[00:28:05] Q: What does بُكْرَة mean? — A: Literally the early part of the morning, hence tomorrow; مُبَكِّر means early.
[00:44:01] Q: Does the لَام drop the نُون the same way أَنْ does? — A: Yes, exactly the same rule, because the لَام also puts the verb into the accusative.
[00:19:00] Q: What is the difference between مَكْتَب and مَكْتَبَة? — A: مَكْتَب is an office; مَكْتَبَة is a library or a bookshop.

quiz.q: What does أَنْ do to a singular verb such as يَذْهَبُ?
options: Gives it a fatḥa — أَنْ يَذْهَبَ
quiz.a: The default effect: the مُضَارِع is put into the accusative.

quiz.q: What happens to يَذْهَبُونَ after أَنْ?
options: It becomes يَذْهَبُوا — the نُون is dropped
quiz.a: There is no room for a fatḥa on an ending already fixed, so the نُون falls away.

quiz.q: Which form does NOT change after أَنْ?
quiz.a: يَذْهَبْنَ carries نُون النِّسْوَة, which is مَبْنِي — nothing alters it.

quiz.q: What becomes of the dual يَذْهَبَانِ after أَنْ?
quiz.a: The dual loses its نُون too, as in يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ.

quiz.q: What becomes of تَذْهَبِينَ after أَنْ?
quiz.a: A single female is still subject to the rule, so the نُون goes: أَنْ تَذْهَبِي.

quiz.q: How many distinct effects can أَنْ have on a verb?
options: Two — a fatḥa, or the dropping of the نُون
quiz.a: The teacher reduced it to exactly these two outcomes, with the feminine plural as the lone exception.

quiz.q: Does لَام التَّعْلِيل follow the same rule?
options: No, it has no effect on the verb
Yes — it also gives a fatḥa or drops the نُون
quiz.a: لِيَعْلَمُوا rather than لِيَعْلَمُونَ — the same mechanism, since both put the verb in the accusative.

options: Because اسْمِي already means my name is, so أَنَا makes it I, my name is
quiz.a: The subject of the sentence is the name, not the speaker, so the pronoun is redundant and wrong.

quiz.a: Hence مُبَكِّر for early, and the Prophet's ﷺ duʿā' for barakah in the ummah's بُكُور.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالُوا إِنْ هَٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا
quran_examples.transliteration: qālū in hādhāni la-sāḥirāni yurīdāni an yukhrijākum min arḍikum bi-siḥrihimā
quran_examples.translation: They said: These two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land by their magic.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's central example: the dual يُخْرِجَانِ loses its نُون after أَنْ to become يُخْرِجَا. Spoken about Mūsā and Hārūn عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام, and the class worked out from the preceding قَالُوا that it is Pharaoh's chiefs addressing the people.

quran_examples.arabic: وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا ۝ إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-lā taqūlanna li-shayʾin innī fāʿilun dhālika ghadan, illā an yashāʾa llāh
quran_examples.translation: And never say of anything: I will do that tomorrow — except when adding: if Allah wills.
quran_examples.note: Raised when غَدًا came up. It also carries أَنْ with a singular verb taking the fatḥa, يَشَاءَ, and opens with a prohibition.

quran_examples.translation: And exalt Him morning and evening.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for بُكْرَة as the early morning, the time he noted carries barakah; سَبِّحُوا is also on the فَعَّلَ pattern in the plural imperative.

quran_examples.arabic: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا
quran_examples.transliteration: yurīdūna an yakhrujū mina al-nāri wa-mā hum bi-khārijīna minhā
quran_examples.translation: They will wish to come out of the Fire, but they will never come out of it.
quran_examples.note: The masculine plural case of the same rule: يَخْرُجُونَ becomes يَخْرُجُوا, written with the silent alif the teacher pointed out.
